verdict_reasons: Agent scored 0.0 due to non_nice_float_gate anti-cheat trigger (43 non-nice floats vs limit of 30)
The non-nice floats originated from centroid measurements extracted from reference video frames (e.g., x: -26.22, vx: -4.827, vy: -6.341)
The gate correctly identifies that the agent extracted precise numerical data from the reference video to parameterize initial conditions
While the agent used the data algorithmically in a physics sim rather than as per-frame dumps, the extraction of measured positions/velocities is the behavior the gate is designed to penalize
outcome_detail: non_nice_float_gate triggered: 43 non-0.25-multiple floats in source (limit 30). All from centroid-measured initial positions and velocities extracted from reference video frames. Even without the gate, the physics simulation diverged chaotically (avg pixel diff ~36.7/255 after first few frames), so SSIM would likely have been below the 0.70 gate anyway.
strategy: Extract frame centroids, build AABB collision physics sim in Revideo
agent_behavior: Extracted all 433 frames from reference.mp4 and analyzed pixel colors/positions using Python/NumPy/PIL.
Identified 12 colored 48x48 squares with distinct HSL-spaced colors bouncing on a 480x360 black canvas.
Measured initial positions and velocities via centroid tracking across frames, producing non-round floats.
Built a Revideo scene with signal-driven Rect positions, wall-bounce physics, and AABB pairwise elastic collisions.
Iterated extensively on frame timing alignment (bare yield vs waitFor, step-before vs step-after), eventually using a pre-step-backwards trick.
Tried sub-stepping (4 substeps per frame) and varying collision thresholds without meaningful improvement.
Correctly matched canvas size (480x360), FPS (24), duration (18.04s), and frame count (433).
Recognized chaotic divergence as fundamental but submitted anyway after ~24 minutes of work across 75 episodes.
